transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Let's get started. As we all know, we've received a deficiency letter from the regulator regarding our marketed pediatric monitoring device, and our written response is due in 30 calendar days. The draft response has been circulated internally but hasn't been approved or submitted yet. We have several unresolved issues to address — software scope, lot disposition, the pediatric indication, and the patient-data fields to be included. I'd like to work through each of these systematically today so we can finalize and approve the response well before the deadline. Who would like to start by walking us through where we stand on the software scope question?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before we go further on the software scope question, I need to flag something important. After our technical call with the regulator, I received a written follow-up message that I saved in the regulatory mailbox but haven't yet incorporated into the circulated draft. The regulator confirmed two key constraints: first, our response must be limited specifically to software version 4.2 — not a broader software scope — and second, the response must include an answer matrix with exactly six question rows. We need to make sure the draft is restructured to meet both of these requirements before we go any further in finalizing it.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical privacy issue before we finalize the patient-data fields section. My privacy review of the regulator's requested data confirmed that the submission may contain only deidentified aggregate data, with suppression of every reporting cell representing fewer than 10 patients. The circulated draft currently does not specify either of these restrictions. We must build both the deidentification requirement and the small-cell suppression threshold into our response before it is approved and submitted.
